_speaker.bio: Sanket Modi maintains roughly 100 hardened, open source container images, rebuilt daily and kept current through continuous version upgrades and proactive CVE remediation—so the teams consuming them inherit a clean foundation instead of a vulnerability backlog. His work centers on a single idea: most container CVEs come from the base image, not the application, so the durable fix belongs upstream, at the foundation, where it can be made once instead of patched everywhere. Over 14 years spanning SDET, DevOps, DevSecOps, and engineering management, he has moved from testing and operating systems to building the secure foundations other teams build on, and now leads community efforts at CleanStart Security. He spoke on container security at KCD Delhi 2026, and regularly writes and runs community sessions on supply-chain integrity, image hardening, and reducing security toil for developers. He believes the best security is invisible—embedded in the foundation so teams focus on shipping products, not managing CVE queues. KCD Delhi was a first step toward larger cloud native stages.

His work focuses on understanding the trust boundaries introduced by AI integrations, particularly where authentication, authorization, and user-controlled input intersect with large language models. Through hands-on research and offensive testing of his own systems, he explores how seemingly ordinary engineering decisions can create significant security risks in LLM-powered applications.

At this session, Harshit shares practical findings from building and breaking real-world AI security tooling, demonstrating how identity propagation failures, authorization gaps, and prompt injection risks emerge in modern SOC environments—and, more importantly, how to fix them.

Maithily Rajpure is a Computer Engineering student specializing in Cybersecurity and an AI Engineering Intern at IIT Bombay's Trust Lab, where she works on secure AI systems for Security Operations Centers (SOCs). Her work focuses on LLM security, authorization, trust boundaries, and building practical AI-powered security tooling.

She is a contributor to queryCopilot, an open-source Kibana plugin that enables analysts to investigate security logs using natural language. While building it, her team uncovered subtle but critical security flaws involving MCP-based architectures, identity propagation, authorization bypasses, and prompt injection in real-world SOC workflows.

At DevRoom, Maithily will share lessons learned from breaking and hardening their own system, demonstrating why the biggest security risks in AI-powered infrastructure often come not from the model itself, but from overlooked assumptions about identity, permissions, and trust boundaries.

You will find him talking on open-source, supply chain security, cloud-native technologies, and community building. He actively mentor and guide new contributors, helping them navigate and grow in the open-source ecosystem.
